pew-politics-2023.name: Pew Research Center: Americans' Dismal Views of the Nation's Politics (U.S., 2023)

exhausted.name: Always or often feel exhausted when thinking about politics
exhausted.passage: nearly two-thirds of Americans (65%) say they always or often feel exhausted when thinking about politics, while 55% feel angry

angry.name: Always or often feel angry when thinking about politics

hopeful.name: Always or often feel hopeful about politics
hopeful.passage: just 10% say they always or often feel hopeful about politics, and even fewer (4%) are excited

district-influence.name: People in members' own districts have too little influence on Congress
district-influence.passage: People in members’ own districts, by contrast, are widely viewed as having too little influence (70% say this).

donor-influence.name: Big campaign donors and lobbyists have too much influence
donor-influence.passage: Large majorities say big campaign donors (80%) and lobbyists and special interests (73%) have too much influence on decisions made by members of Congress.

voting-matters.name: Voting by people like me can affect the country’s future direction
voting-matters.passage: Nearly six-in-ten (57%) say voting by people like them can affect the country’s future direction, though just 20% say it can affect this a lot.

uk-community-life-2024-25.name: UK Community Life Survey 2024/25: civic engagement and social action (England)

influence-local-decisions.name: Can personally influence decisions affecting the local area
influence-local-decisions.passage: 24% of adults agreed (either “definitely” or “tended” to agree) that they can personally influence decisions affecting their local area.

want-more-involved.name: Would like to be more involved in decisions made by the council
want-more-involved.passage: 28% of adults said that they would like to be more involved in decisions made by their council that affect the local area

civic-activism.name: Civic activism: local roles such as councillor, school governor or magistrate
civic-activism.passage: 8% of adults had engaged in civic activism at least once in the last 12 months in 2024/25.

social-action.name: Involved in wider social action
social-action.passage: 13% of adults in 2024/25 reported being involved in wider social action activities at least once in the last 12 months

uk-community-life-volunteering-2024-25.name: UK Community Life Survey 2024/25: barriers to formal volunteering (England)

other-things.name: I do other things in my spare time
other-things.passage: ‘I do other things in my spare time’ – 32%

look-after-children.name: I have to look after children

census-cev-2023.name: U.S. Census Bureau and AmeriCorps: Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement, 2023

formal-volunteering.name: Volunteered through an organization
formal-volunteering.passage: The estimated 28.3% of Americans who reported volunteering through an organization in the previous year in the latest survey is up from 23.2% in 2021.

hours-per-volunteer.name: Hours served per volunteer
hours-per-volunteer.passage: Nationally, average hours served per volunteer in the previous year dropped from 96.5 hours when the CEV began in 2017 to 70 hours in 2023.

informal-helping.name: Helped or exchanged favors with neighbors
informal-helping.passage: An estimated 54.2% of Americans helped or exchanged favors with neighbors such as house sitting, running errands, or lending tools

trust-gap.name: Trust in charities before giving
trust-gap.passage: While 67.7% of respondents say it is essential to trust a charity before donating, only 18.3% report having high trust in charities.

give-if-asked.name: Might give more if asked
give-if-asked.passage: This includes 27.9% who say they might be willing to give more if asked and 14.1% who would like charities to approach them more.

repower-organizers-2022.name: re:power organizer survey (2022), as excerpted from The Nation

burnout.name: Burnout among organizers
burnout.passage: The poll found that burnout, low pay, and institutional barriers to seizing power make up a trifecta of issues facing organizers at all time scales.

low-pay.name: Low pay for organizers
low-pay.passage: burnout, low pay, and institutional barriers to seizing power

institutional-barriers.name: Institutional barriers to seizing power
institutional-barriers.passage: burnout, low pay, and institutional barriers to seizing power

brennan-officeholders-2024.name: Brennan Center: Intimidation of State and Local Officeholders (2024)

abuse-local.name: Local officeholders facing threats, attacks, insults or harassment
abuse-local.passage: The numbers balloon to 89 percent of state legislators and 52 percent of local officeholders when less severe forms of abuse — insults or harassment such as stalking — are included.

less-willing-to-run.name: Less willing to run again because of abuse
less-willing-to-run.passage: More than 40 percent of local officeholders said they were less willing to run for reelection or higher office at the time they were surveyed because of abuse.

controversial-topics.name: Less willing to work on controversial topics because of abuse
controversial-topics.passage: Approximately 20 percent of state officeholders and 40 percent of local officeholders acknowledged they were less willing to work on controversial topics due to abuse.

gallup-mip.name: Gallup: most important problem facing the country, items about leadership and acting together (September 2026)

ipsos-www.name: Ipsos What Worries the World (January 2026), direction of the country and corruption

wrong-track.name: Country heading off on the wrong track

oecd-wellbeing.name: OECD Well-being Framework: Civic engagement, and the OECD Trust Survey 2024 (oecd.org returned 403; UN Statistics and Living Library copies)

have-a-say.name: Having a say in what the government does
have-a-say.passage: The trust gap is largest between those who feel they have a say and those who feel they do not have a say in what the government does.

sdg-targets.name: UN SDG targets bearing on taking part and acting together

16.7.passage: Ensure responsive, inclusive, participatory and representative decision-making at all levels

16.10.passage: Ensure public access to information and protect fundamental freedoms, in accordance with national legislation and international agreements

17.17.passage: Encourage and promote effective public, public-private and civil society partnerships

11.3.passage: enhance inclusive and sustainable urbanization and capacity for participatory, integrated and sustainable human settlement planning and management in all countries

5.5.passage: Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making in political, economic and public life

participation.name: Participation
participation.passage: become affiliated, cooperate, propose, share, dissent, obey, interact, agree on, express opinions

creation.name: Creation
creation.passage: passion, determination, intuition, imagination, boldness, rationality, autonomy, inventiveness, curiosity

community.name: Community Well-Being
community.passage: The fifth element is about the sense of engagement you have with the area where you live: your Community Well-Being
